Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:45:53 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Cebu City Demands Flood Mitigation Plans from Upland Developers https://beesayatv.com/cebu-city-demands-flood-mitigation-plans-from-upland-developers/ Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:45:53 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1264

The Cebu City Government is cracking down on upland property developers, demanding they submit comprehensive flood mitigation plans to address worsening water runoff in lowland communities.

According to city officials, out of the 65 developers operating in the city’s mountain barangays, only four met the initial deadline to submit their requirements. Officials cited the loss of natural soil absorption due to extensive upland concrete construction as a direct cause of severe downstream flooding.

Developers were given an extended deadline of August 27 to provide exact details of their detention ponds and water catchment facilities to prove their hillside projects can properly manage stormwater.

For hikers and outdoor enthusiasts exploring Cebu City’s upland areas, the ongoing developer crackdown highlights how rapid mountain construction and altered natural waterways continue to reshape the local environment and trail ecosystems.

Photo: Cebu City Public Information Office

Source: CDN Digital / The Manila Times

]]> Why Trail Reports and Videos Are Stripped of the Creator’s Feeling https://beesayatv.com/why-trail-reports-and-videos-are-stripped-of-the-creators-feeling/ Tue, 25 Aug 2026 04:26:08 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1250

beesayatv trail reports and videos are intentionally stripped of the creator’s feelings.

I see this project as an archive rather than an adventure channel. The purpose is to document and map Cebu’s changing trail networks as objectively as possible.

Trails change. Paths disappear, new routes emerge, vegetation takes over, roads are built, and communities expand. What exists today may not exist in the same form years from now. The footage is therefore a record of what was actually there when I passed through.

The Trail Is the Main Character

Did I suffer in the mountains? Of course.

There are difficult climbs, heat, exhaustion, uncertainty, and uncomfortable moments. But those are my experiences, not necessarily characteristics of the trail.

The main character is not my ego.

It is the trail.

Personal feelings, discomfort, and drama are therefore deliberately kept out of the documentation. The more I make the hike about myself, the more I place an emotional filter between the viewer and the landscape.

Removing that filter allows the trail to speak for itself.

No Music, No Manufactured Emotion

The absence of dramatic narration and background music is intentional.

Music can tell the viewer when something is beautiful, dangerous, exciting, or emotional. Narration can tell them how they are supposed to interpret what they see.

I would rather let the environment provide that information.

Footsteps, wind, birds, insects, water, motorcycles, distant voices, and other natural sounds are part of the field record. They do not need to be replaced with a soundtrack.

A Sterile Approach

The resulting videos may feel “sterile.” That is deliberate.

I approach the mountains more like a field observer than a performer. The trail, landscape, sounds, structures, vegetation, and surrounding communities are the subjects being documented.

In this sense, I treat trail networks almost like public infrastructure or a scientific subject: something to be observed, mapped, and recorded rather than turned into a story about me.

This does not mean the hikes are emotionless. It means the emotions belong to me, while the trail belongs in the archive.

My job is not to become the story.

My job is to preserve the story of the place.

]]> Danao City Warns Hikers Against Completing 5 Peaks in One Day https://beesayatv.com/danao-city-warns-hikers-against-completing-5-peaks-in-one-day/ Mon, 10 Aug 2026 05:44:54 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1210

The Danao City Tourism and Development Office is reminding hikers that completing all five peaks of the Danao City 5 Peaks Eco Trail Circuit in a single day is not recommended or permitted as part of its official hiking activities.

According to the tourism office, the guideline applies regardless of a hiker’s experience level. Officials cited the terrain, elevation, trail conditions, changing weather, and considerable distances between the peaks as safety concerns.

Hikers are encouraged to follow the city’s recommended day-trip itineraries instead of attempting multiple peaks beyond the prescribed route.

The tourism office also recommends booking hikes directly through its office, where registered City Guides are assigned and routes, safety monitoring, and barangay coordination can be arranged.

For hikers planning to explore Danao’s mountain trails, the advisory is a reminder to check the official itinerary before attempting a multi-peak route.

Photo: Danao City Tourism FB Page

Source: Danao City Tourism and Development Office
Danao City Tourism Facebook page

]]> Talisay Probes Attempted Illegal Waste Dumping in Jaclupan https://beesayatv.com/talisay-probes-attempted-illegal-waste-dumping-in-jaclupan/ Sat, 08 Aug 2026 22:46:48 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1204

Talisay City authorities are investigating an attempted illegal waste disposal incident in Sitio Tabok Sapa, Barangay Jaclupan, after a contractor and truck driver were intercepted on August 3 while allegedly attempting to dump garbage in the area.

Mayor Samsam Gullas said the City would pursue appropriate cases against those found responsible.

The waste reportedly came from Waterworld Cebu Philippines Corp. On August 7, the resort apologized, saying it learned about the incident through social media and was deeply sorry for the concern it caused.

The incident highlights the importance of proper waste disposal, particularly in Cebu’s upland communities, where illegal dumping can threaten waterways and surrounding natural areas.

Photo: SunStar Cebu

]]> Cebu City to Review Drainage Plan Following Widespread Flooding https://beesayatv.com/cebu-city-to-review-drainage-plan-following-widespread-flooding/ Mon, 03 Aug 2026 23:59:34 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1197

Following the July 30 flooding, Cebu City plans to acquire a one-hectare property in the Tisa-Labangon area to serve as a floodwater reservoir while reviewing its 2017 Drainage Master Plan.

City officials said narrowed waterways, garbage-clogged drainage, and increased runoff from upland developments have contributed to flooding in downstream communities. Some natural channels that were once six to 10 feet wide have reportedly narrowed to around three feet, reducing their capacity to carry stormwater during heavy rain.

The proposed reservoir is intended to temporarily store excess rainwater before it reaches flood-prone communities. The City also plans to inspect upland developments to determine whether additional catchment facilities are needed to better manage runoff.

For hikers and outdoor enthusiasts, the announcement serves as a reminder that what happens in Cebu’s uplands can directly affect rivers, road conditions, and communities downstream. Watersheds extend far beyond individual trails, making responsible land use and drainage management important to both public safety and the natural environments.

Source: SunStar Cebu, Shrinking rivers fuel city floods, August 3, 2026.

]]> Fruit Trees and Plants Along the Trail https://beesayatv.com/fruit-trees-and-plants-along-the-trail/ Sat, 01 Aug 2026 22:45:10 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1192

Fruit trees and useful plants are common along mountain roads and community trails.

Mangoes, guavas, coconuts, malunggay, and other herbs may grow close to the path, sometimes without fences or any visible house nearby.

For hikers coming from the city, seeing fruit still hanging from the tree can be part of the experience.

It is not something seen every day, and even a small guava or mango can become an interesting detail to photograph or include in a hiking video.

Visible Does Not Mean Unowned

A tree beside the trail may appear wild or unattended.

In many cases, however, it was planted by a nearby household, farmer, or landowner. The area around it may not look like a formal farm, but the tree can still be maintained, harvested, or reserved for personal use.

The same applies to malunggay and other plants growing along fences, roadsides, and the edges of private land.

Their owners may not be visible when hikers pass through.

Farmers and residents have other work to do and cannot watch every tree or plant throughout the day. Their absence should not be understood as permission to take something.

Picking Without Asking

Some hiking videos show people picking fruit directly from branches or gathering herbs along the route.

A single fruit may appear insignificant, especially when many others remain on the tree.

The situation changes when a trail becomes popular and several groups begin doing the same thing. What looks harmless when done once can become repeated taking from the same property.

The hiker may pass through only once, but the person who planted the tree or maintains the land continues to live there.

Without clear permission, it is difficult to know whether the fruit is meant for the household, for selling, for feeding animals, or simply for harvesting later.

Looking Without Taking

Fruit trees can still be appreciated without removing anything from them.

During fieldwork, fruit may be photographed, shown in video, or briefly held while it remains attached to the branch.

This captures the experience of encountering it along the route without assuming that it is available to take.

There are also practical reasons not to eat fruit found along the trail. It may be difficult to wash properly, and wild-growing fruit such as guava can sometimes be too small or not yet ready.

The more important reason, however, is respect for the land and the people connected to it.

Passing Through Someone Else’s Space

Many hiking routes pass through farms, residential areas, and working landscapes.

They may feel open because there are no gates, signs, or people standing nearby, but they are not empty spaces.

The trees, plants, fences, water sources, and crops encountered along the route may all be part of someone’s daily life and livelihood.

Hikers are usually only passing through.

Seeing fruit on the tree can be a memorable part of the hike. Leaving it where it is allows the next passerby to see it as well and, more importantly, respects the person who may have planted and cared for it.

]]> Temporary Waterfalls Appear Along Manipis Road After Days of Rain https://beesayatv.com/temporary-waterfalls-appear-along-manipis-road-after-days-of-rain/ Sat, 01 Aug 2026 12:58:19 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1187

Status: Field conditions update

Several temporary waterfalls were observed along Manipis Road in Talisay City on the morning of August 1, 2026, following days of regular rainfall in the uplands.

No major landslide or road blockage was seen during the field check. In previous periods of prolonged rain, some sections of Manipis Road had become impassable due to landslides and fallen debris.

Water was instead flowing heavily from several mountain slopes beside the road. Drainage channels and catchment basins have been constructed in many of these areas, indicating that runoff regularly passes through them during wet weather.

These roadside cascades are normally dry during fair weather but become active after several days of rain as water collected in the mountains flows downhill. Much of the runoff eventually reaches the Mananga River.

The river was also carrying a noticeably stronger flow. While the water level was not exceptionally high, the current was sufficient to cover sections of the riverbed that are normally visible during dry conditions.

Motorists and visitors passing through Manipis Road should remain cautious, as slope conditions and water flow may change quickly when rainfall continues in the uplands.

Video: BeesayaTV field documentation

Source: BeesayaTV field observation along Manipis Road and Mananga River, August 1, 2026.

]]> Alegria Suspends River-Related Tourism Activities Due to Weather Risks https://beesayatv.com/alegria-suspends-river-related-tourism-activities-due-to-weather-risks/ Fri, 31 Jul 2026 21:48:34 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1176

Status: Temporary safety suspension

All river-related eco-tourism activities in Alegria, Cebu have been temporarily suspended beginning July 31, 2026, according to an advisory from the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.

The suspension will remain in effect until further notice due to prevailing weather conditions that may cause sudden increases in river levels and flash floods. Tourism operators, guides, visitors, and other concerned groups were instructed to comply with the advisory.

The order may affect visits and guided activities around Alegria’s waterfalls, natural pools, rivers, and canyoneering areas. These potentially include Cambais Falls, Cangkalanog Falls, and routes beginning along the Kanlaob and Cancalapi river systems. Some Alegria canyoneering routes continue downstream toward Kawasan Falls in neighboring Badian.

Hikers and outdoor visitors planning routes near rivers, waterfalls, or stream crossings should postpone river-based activities and check official local updates before travelling. Trails that cross waterways may also become unsafe even when rainfall is occurring farther upstream.

The resumption of activities will be announced through the official channels of the Municipal Government of Alegria.

Photo: MDRRMO Alegria FB Page

Source: MDRRMO Alegria. Temporary suspension of all river-related eco-tourism activities. Posted July 31, 2026.

]]> 162 Green Sea Turtle Hatchlings Reach Sea in Panglao, Bohol https://beesayatv.com/162-green-sea-turtle-hatchlings-reach-sea-in-panglao-bohol/ Fri, 31 Jul 2026 00:29:25 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1164

Status: Wildlife conservation update

A total of 162 endangered green sea turtle hatchlings reached the sea after emerging from a protected nest along Alona Beach in Barangay Tawala, Panglao, Bohol. The nest contained 192 eggs and had been monitored for 49 days by environmental personnel and local partners.

The nesting site was monitored by DENR Central Visayas with assistance from local government offices, the Philippine Coast Guard, nearby establishments, and volunteers. Beachfront properties were also asked to reduce artificial lighting and avoid flash photography, as bright lights may disorient hatchlings moving toward the water.

For visitors to Panglao and other coastal areas, the event highlights the importance of keeping nesting sites undisturbed. Artificial lights, crowds, and activity near protected nests may affect hatchlings during their movement from the beach to the sea.

Photo: DENR Central Visayas

Source: DENR Central Visayas and The Freeman. Reports on 162 green sea turtle hatchlings in Panglao, Bohol. Retrieved July 2026.

]]> Oslob LGU Schedules Tree Planting Following Backlash Over Felled Plaza Trees https://beesayatv.com/oslob-lgu-schedules-tree-planting-following-backlash-over-felled-plaza-trees/ Fri, 31 Jul 2026 00:11:21 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1159

Status: Reforestation and Watershed Notice

The Municipal Government of Oslob has scheduled a public tree-planting activity on Friday, July 31, 2026, from 5:30 AM to 7:30 AM in Upper Barangay Nueva Caceres. Participants will assemble at the Oslob Municipal Hall Grounds before heading to the site. According to the LGU, the initiative serves as a replacement program for trees cleared for the new Oslob Sports and Cultural Complex, aiming to boost local tree cover, protect watersheds, and prevent soil erosion.

The replacement drive follows public criticism and regulatory action by DENR Region 7, which cited the municipality for cutting 10 trees at the town plaza without prior notice or required permit coordination, prompting CENRO Argao to prepare a cease and desist order. Local heritage advocates and residents had raised alarm over the destruction of mature shade trees in the town core.

For hikers, trail runners, and conservation-minded readers heading through Southern Cebu, reforestation in Upper Nueva Caceres directly impacts the health of the surrounding upland watershed and slope stability. Oslobanons and local eco-advocates interested in supporting municipal tree cover are encouraged to join the early morning activity.

Photo: LGU Oslob Facebook Page

Source: SunStar Cebu and LGU Oslob Facebook Page. LGU Oslob Tree Planting Activity Announcement. Retrieved July 2026.
